conditions: The statement has catch clauses with no finally block or resource specification.
The try block throws, and at least one catch clause has a catchable exception class to which the thrown value's run-time type is assignment compatible.
limitations: The rule selects a handler for a throw from the try block. The selected catch block's completion follows its own rule.

triggers: Exact-edition correction, retrieval identity change, or material scope challenge.

statement: When the try block of an ordinary try-catch statement throws a value, Java SE 21 selects the first catch clause in source order for which the value's run-time type is assignment compatible with a catchable exception class.
